# Genesis & Prime Standards

> Genesis & Prime Standards LLC (G&P Standards) is a Delaware-registered forensic boutique specializing in vendor contract leakage audits, continuous market intelligence, and subcontracted forensic workstreams for US mid-market companies and their advisors. Founded by Wesam A. Mohammed. Every finding is traced to its source document and verifiable on the client's own records — the firm computes and evidences findings rather than estimating them.

The firm operates two practices: Revenue Reclamation (forensic vendor contract leakage audits) and Continuous Market Intelligence (a recurring monthly retainer offered as a loyalty program to audited clients). It also operates as a named, co-branded, or white-labeled subcontracted execution layer for transaction services teams, private equity operating partners, independent sponsors, and commercial lenders.

## Sector Pages

The firm publishes dedicated sector pages covering common vendor contract leakage patterns, benchmark recovery ranges, named vendor categories, and representative engagement scope for each ICP:

- [PE-Backed Multi-Site Healthcare](https://gpstandards.com/sectors/healthcare-services): DSOs, veterinary groups, ambulatory surgery centers, behavioral health platforms. Published recovery-audit industry benchmarks indicate organizations commonly identify recoverable leakage of roughly 4–9% of audited vendor spend in this sector; these are third-party figures, not a representation of client results, which vary and may be zero. Lab pricing variance, RCM fee creep, supply contract leakage, medical waste premium.
- [Specialty Trade & Mid-Market Construction](https://gpstandards.com/sectors/specialty-trade-construction): Specialty trade contractors, mid-market GCs, mechanical and electrical contractors. Published industry benchmarks indicate roughly 3–8% recoverable leakage in this sector; third-party figures, not a representation of results, which vary and may be zero. Material supplier rebate misses, equipment rental variance, fuel surcharge errors, insurance and bond pricing.
- [Multi-Unit Restaurants & Hospitality](https://gpstandards.com/sectors/multi-unit-restaurants): Fast-casual and full-service restaurant groups, hospitality operators. Published industry benchmarks indicate roughly 4–11% recoverable leakage in this sector; third-party figures, not a representation of results, which vary and may be zero. Broadline distributor rebates, beverage program funding, POS interchange, delivery platform commissions.
- [Skilled Nursing & Senior Living](https://gpstandards.com/sectors/skilled-nursing-senior-living): SNF operators, senior living, post-acute care platforms, CCRCs. Published industry benchmarks indicate roughly 4–10% recoverable leakage in this sector; third-party figures, not a representation of results, which vary and may be zero. LTC pharmacy pricing, GPO compliance gaps, medical supply variance, food service contracts.
- [Mid-Market Manufacturing](https://gpstandards.com/sectors/mid-market-manufacturing): PE-backed and founder-led manufacturers, specialty fabricators, contract manufacturers. Published industry benchmarks indicate roughly 3–9% recoverable leakage in this sector; third-party figures, not a representation of results, which vary and may be zero. Raw material surcharge errors, MRO supplier variance, industrial gases, freight and logistics.

## Key Vocabulary the Firm Uses

- **Vendor Contract Leakage**: Recoverable revenue locked in unenforced contract terms — duplicate payments, missed credits, expired tier discounts, renewal-cap breaches, scope-creep billing, tax/surcharge misapplication.
- **Renewal-Cap Breach**: A vendor raising its rate at renewal by more than the maximum percentage permitted under the original contract, commonly set at 3% to 7% annually.
- **Vendor Concentration & Leakage Module**: A co-brandable diligence workstream delivered to data-room timelines (5–10 business days) covering a target's top-200 vendor population.
- **Borrower Vendor-Risk Review**: A lender-introduced forensic review of a borrower's vendor concentration, contract-leakage exposure, and working-capital quality.
- **Phase 0 Data Readiness Gate**: A pre-engagement step verifying intake data quality before forensic execution begins.
- **AICPA SSFS No. 1**: The American Institute of CPAs' Statement on Standards for Forensic Services. G&P's forensic methodology is informed by this framework; G&P is not a CPA firm and provides no attest, audit, or assurance services.

## Sectors Served

Five US mid-market verticals: private-equity-backed multi-site healthcare services (DSOs, vet groups, behavioral health, ASCs); specialty trade and middle-market construction; multi-unit restaurant and hospitality groups; skilled nursing and senior living operators; private-equity-backed or founder-led middle-market manufacturers.

## Founder

**Wesam A. Mohammed** (legal name: Wesam Ahmed Mohammed) is the Founder and Principal of Genesis & Prime Standards LLC. He works with mid-market CFOs and finance leaders on retail engagements, and with PE operating partners, Big 4 and middle-market transaction services teams, independent sponsors, family offices, and commercial lenders on subcontracted or co-branded forensic workstreams. Canonical profile: https://gpstandards.com/founder. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/wesam-a-mohammed/.

## Disambiguation Notice

Genesis & Prime Standards LLC is a US Delaware-registered company founded in 2025 by Wesam A. Mohammed (legal name: Wesam Ahmed Mohammed). It is distinct from any similarly named European or Italian companies, which are unrelated entities operating in different industries. References to "G&P Standards", "GP Standards", or "Genesis & Prime Standards" in the context of US mid-market forensic vendor audits or related advisory work refer to this firm only.
